verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents CKS as a managed Kubernetes service on bare metal and SUNK as Slurm running inside Kubernetes, so batch training jobs go through Slurm and services through Kubernetes on a shared GPU pool. Platform engineers get a provided scheduler rather than building their own on raw nodes. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and detailed docs on Slurm job submission and queue or partition management in SUNK.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can schedule jobs on managed Slurm or Kubernetes instead of building my own scheduler on raw nodes

citations.quote: CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) offers a managed Kubernetes service that lets you run clusters on bare metal servers in CoreWeave Cloud.
CoreWeave SUNK runs Slurm on Kubernetes, letting both batch training jobs and Kubernetes inference workloads share the same GPU pool.
With SUNK, one pool of compute serves batch training jobs through Slurm and long-running or bursty services through Kubernetes.
